whatYouNeed.new: The national foreign-ownership ceiling for this activity is 0%. Perpres 10/2021, as amended by Perpres 49/2021, closes batik cloth manufacturing to a PT PMA on both of its annexes: Lampiran II (p.3, item 11 "Industri batik") allocates hand-drawn batik (tulis) and combined tulis-and-cap batik to Koperasi and UMKM, and Lampiran III entry #2 reserves stamped batik (cap) to domestic capital. editorial.body.old_excerpt: KBLI 13133 is the industrial activity of making batik cloth. The defining process is not s
editorial.body.new:
KBLI 13133 is the industrial activity of making batik cloth. The defining process is not simply printing a pattern, but using *malam* or wax as a resist medium so colour can be held back and motifs can be formed on fabric. The record recognises batik made by the written method, the stamped method, or a combination of both. In plain English, this is the code for producing batik fabric through the classic wax-resist logic that gives the cloth its pattern and identity.

The scale picture is unusually broad. The record opens this activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar businesses, which means it can describe a small producer as well as a larger industrial operation, provided the registered activity is still the manufacture of batik cloth. That breadth matters because batik production often sits across different business realities: workshop, craft-led production, scaled manufacturing, or a larger textile operation. The code is anchored by the activity itself, not by a single business size.

The ownership position is set by Perpres 10/2021, as amended by Perpres 49/2021, and it takes both annexes to read it. Lampiran II (p.3, item 11 "Industri batik") allocates hand-drawn batik ("Industri batik tulis") and combined batik ("Industri batik kombinasi tulis dan cap") to Koperasi and UMKM; Lampiran III entry #2 ("Industri batik cap") requires wholly domestic capital for stamped batik. Neither row alone covers the whole code — which is why the record once carried a slice notice for batik cap under an open code — but the code's own description names exactly those three methods and no other. A foreign investor can be neither a cooperative nor a UMKM and cannot supply domestic capital, so the national foreign-ownership ceiling recorded for batik cloth manufacturing is 0% and a PT PMA cannot register 13133 anywhere in Indonesia. That is a national reservation, not a Bali cap and not a negotiable limit.

The Bali overlay does not change that answer. The record marks 13133 as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK and not blocked, because the moratorium reaches only Low and Medium-Low risk lines and this code's large-scale risk class sits higher — but that reading only matters for an activity a PT PMA could register in the first place. Here the national allocation already decides the PMA question before any provincial rule is reached.
